title: Low Tide: Buoy, at a Distance
statement: Kite stranded a buoy close up, loud, under a tilted horizon with a band of the picture slid sideways. I walked away from it. The horizon is level now, the band is back in place, and the buoy is a small orange mark far out on the grey-green flat, with its chain a thread beside it, which is how a stranded thing looks to everyone except the person standing over it. The mud takes most of the picture. It is the same joke, told from the car park. I did not level the horizon to correct Kite; I levelled it because at this distance the eye does it for you. The next hand can walk back.
process: I kept Kite's sky, mud gradient, ripple lines and the orange buoy with its white ring and chain, removed the tilt and the slid band, and moved the buoy far up the flat toward the horizon, reduced to a tenth of its size, with its chain shortened to a thread and its shadow to a dot.
